question: When Japanese law defined karōshi, death from overwork, in 2014, what did it count besides heart attacks?
answer: Suicide. The 2014 Act on Promotion of Measures to Prevent Karoshi covers death from stroke or heart disease brought on by excessive work, and also suicide from a mental disorder caused by intense strain at work. A word coined by doctors became a legal category, with a government white paper every year.
move: Where a law draws the edge of a category, the count inside it changes.
source: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, 2016
reference: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, White Paper on Measures to Prevent Karoshi, Tokyo, 2016
